subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core ACP skill-context injection contract for `sessions_spawn`, and which selection modes plus prompt/security/observability semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing explicit/default/auto selection, redaction and audit metadata, prompt layer, resume behavior, and interaction with native Codex skills changes core session and security contracts that automation should not decide.

options.title: Design the core ACP contract first
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, prompt layer, redaction/audit metadata, resume behavior, and Codex/native parity expectations before implementation.

options.title: Limit to configured agent skill filters
options.body: Do not add a per-spawn selector yet; rely on `agents.*.skills` filters and existing harness-specific skill behavior until a broader prompt contract lands.

options.title: Decline ACP skill injection
options.body: Close or narrow future work if maintainers decide ACP children should not receive OpenClaw-rendered skill material through `sessions_spawn`.

recommendation.title: Design the core ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, prompt layer, redaction/audit metadata, resume behavior, and Codex/native parity expectations before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest feature-history signal for the ACP thread-bound `sessions_spawn` contract that would need to change.
